newsitem.title: THAILAND: Key personalities in Thai politics.
newsitem.headline: Key personalities in Thai politics.

text.p: Here are brief profiles of the two Thai politicians seen most likely to become the next prime minister in the country's election on Sunday.
CHAVALIT YONGCHAIYUDH - An orchestrator of Thai politics for decades both in and out of uniform, General Chavalit, 64, has had a keen eye on the nation's top job.
A former army chief and defence minister in Banharn Silpa-archa's coalition government, Chavalit heads the New Aspiration Party which he helped found in 1990 after retiring from the military.
Since being named Defence Minister after a July, 1995 general election, the ambitious Chavalit has often been touted as one of the candidates to be the next prime minister.

He has been seen using the defence portfolio to strengthen his own power base, managing military reshuffles to place officers loyal to him in key positions and supporting big-budget military procurement to keep favour with the armed forces.
Making no secret of his aspiration to rise to Thailand's top job, Chavalit says he has been a behind-the-scenes power broker for too long and now wants to become prime minister.

CHUAN LEEKPAI - Veteran politician Chuan Leekpai, who as opposition leader doggedly helped topple the previous Thai government, is poised to regain the nation's top job after a lapse of over 16 months.

Considered the darling of the business community, which widely believes he is the only leader who can salvage Thailand's slowing economy, the former premier has wooed supporters by promising to stabilise the economy.

Although Chuan failed to complete his four-year mandate and was forced to dissolve parliament in May 1995, the leader of the Democrat Party made history by becoming the the country's longest-serving democratically-elected premier.

Chuan, a shy, soft-spoken and youthful-looking 58-year old, was ousted as prime minister after his party became embroiled in a land scandal and faced with loss of support he was forced to call fresh elections in July 1995.
Chuan has won his home province seat 10 times in a row
